story: The creator deity had human appearance and a beard, and ordered the building of a great city, traveling sometimes with companions also called by his name. He rose from a great lake during a time of darkness to bring forth light, making the sun, moon, and stars. He formed humankind by breathing into stones, but his first creation was a race of brainless giants who displeased him; he destroyed them with a flood and made better humans from smaller stones, scattering them across the world. He then disappeared across the ocean, walking upon the water, never to return. He wandered the earth disguised as a beggar, teaching his creations the foundations of civilization and performing miracles, though many refused his teachings and fell into warfare, causing him to weep. It was believed he would return in times of trouble. He was described as a man of medium height, white-skinned, wearing a white robe, carrying a staff and a book. In one telling he had a son and two daughters. He destroyed the people around the great lake with a flood lasting sixty days and nights, sparing two beings, a son of the sun and a woman representing fertility, who carried a golden staff and founded a civilization. In another version he fathered the first eight humans, and had a wife associated with the sea. In yet another legend, he had two sons whom he sent to visit distant tribes to test their obedience, naming plants and teaching which were edible, medicinal, or poisonous. The three eventually reached a city and the seacoast, where they walked across the water and vanished.
